competency_fulfillment.rationale:
Six of eight samples contain no money at all: seed 44's "A class survey showed 90 students like costume sash and 6 students like wristband. How many students were surveyed in all?", seed 45's bare "What is 30 + 45?", and seed 68's "There are 0 cookies.
(Large group of 74 cookies) — 74 more cookies are added.
How many total cookies are there?" all replace the ₱ money context this competency is entirely about.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both named money sub-cases do appear -- subtraction in seed 42 ("Hiro had ₱5 and spent ₱1 on resin at the gaming convention. How much money does Hiro have left?") and addition in seed 43 ("Kuya Bien has ₱1 in bills and ₱5 in coins. How much money does Kuya Bien have in all?") -- but they are only 2 of 8 samples, so the required coverage exists but is thin.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence structures stay short and grade-appropriate throughout, e.g. "Ate Cara has 10 photo albums. A classmate has 5 photo albums. How many more photo albums does Ate Cara have?", regardless of the topic mismatch noted elsewhere.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The apparent 'variation' across the eight samples is mostly a swap to entirely different non-money topics -- student surveys (44, 50, 110), bare arithmetic (45), photo albums (46), and cookies (68) -- rather than varied money-problem framings such as buying, saving, or making change.

competency_alignment.rationale:
Seeds 44, 45, 46, 50, 68, and 110 vary along unrelated axes, e.g. seed 68's cookie count ("There are 0 cookies.
(Large group of 74 cookies) — 74 more cookies are added.") and seed 110's marker-set/tarpaulin survey, instead of building the money addition/subtraction competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The two genuine money samples use only tiny amounts -- ₱5-₱1=₱4 in seed 42 and ₱1+₱5=₱6 in seed 43 -- far short of testing anywhere near the competency's stated ₱100 addition ceiling.
